Definition: a flower of the same name, from νάρκη (stupefaction, as a "narcotic"); Narcissus, a Roman:--Narcissus.
BiblicalUsage: Narcissus is a Roman Christian whose household Paul greets, and his name is all we know of him. In Romans 16:11 Paul says, greet them that be of the household of Narcissus, which are in the Lord, and the greeting is the whole record.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a household in the Lord is a church in miniature, and Narcissus is remembered for the people around his table. Paul does not greet the man himself, which may mean he is already gone, but his household is still in the Lord.
